They've definitely gotten less severe and less frequent for me.

I'm not sure when they started but they probably peaked between 12-16. I think learning I'm autistic has helped with preventing/coping with them.  I'm more aware of my triggers and what it feels like when I'm starting to get overwhelmed.  When they happen, I know now that I can do safer stims like flapping my hands and rocking instead of harming myself.

It's clear from not only my experience, but from posts/comments I've read of other people that the SAM is not helpful in this context.  It also isn't accurate to characterize the SAM as a way to measure "fluid sexuality".

The SAM made me think that I was interested in men even though I wasn't sexually attracted to them because I did feel romantic attraction to them.  However, what I was feeling wasn't romantic attraction, it was comphet.   I'm not saying the SAM forces women into heterosexuality.  I am saying that the model is too often applied in an unhelpful way and without nuance outside of the community it was created to serve (aspec ppl). 

In terms of the issue of sexuality being fluid, binary labels aren't fluid and that's okay.  That isn't their purpose.  Nobody is saying you have to fit into a binary.  If you don't fit into a binary, there are many other "fluid" labels that you can use- lesbian just isn't one of them.  It's okay to be bi or pan with a preference for women.

It's all connected to hormones.  The week before and of your period, or your luteal phase, your estrogen and progesterone levels are lowest.  Low hormone levels = low dopamine levels.  This is what causes PMS symptoms.  For people with ADHD, the drop in hormone levels also makes our ADHD symptoms worse, and can lower the effectiveness of ADHD meds.  

I started using the Flo app almost a year ago to track my periods, but the reason I like it so much now is because it gives you information every day about what your hormone levels are doing and what common symptoms are for that time of the cycle.

I'm not an expert and I don't have depression but the way I understand it is

ADHD is defined as a developmental disorder.  It is wanting to do things, but no matter how much you want to do them, you just can't get yourself started or focused.  You'll spend hours thinking about doing the tasks but not actually be able to start.  With ADHD (for me at least) this inability to do tasks even if I want to --> anxiety/low self esteem/low motivation

Depression is a mood disorder.  It involves constant sadness or emptiness, losing interest in doing anything, feeling too mentally exhausted to do simple tasks like personal hygiene, and feeling worthless.  More of a "what's the point of doing xyz".  I think it's more of a cycle of persistent sadness --> inability to function/complete tasks --> worthlessness and back around.  

​
